entries.content:
It is astonishing, really, how the finger on the button removes itself from the person behind it, as if authority were some vast domestic engine humming in the background—one to which, with trembling hands and polite nervousness, we all attend. My trust, I confess, has developed hairline fractures: not only in the faceless figure behind the desk but in the person who obeyed so neatly, so sensibly, as if shocking a fellow were a minor inconvenience, like forgetting to iron a shirt. Under such pressure, I felt myself folding inward: neat, composed, smiling—yet I caught a glimpse of something furious and sorrowful behind my own glassy obedience.
